rationale: Probe the sourced empty-context read acknowledgment discrepancy with a real election and a fresh-context control, preserving the documented request-loss and retry qualification rather than asserting a universal completion guarantee.

investigations.question: Does an empty ReadIndex context prevent completion in a healthy stable multi-voter leader, and what does the documented fresh-context retry obligation imply for defect applicability?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader queues an empty context and broadcasts it, but skips every resulting empty-context heartbeat acknowledgment. A subsequent nonempty request may release the earlier queued request.
investigations.discriminator: Compare independent empty and nonempty contexts after identical elected-leader prefixes, inspect heartbeat contexts and readStates after message drain and three complete heartbeat rounds, then submit a fresh unique request. Investigate whether the API permits the initial context and whether its explicit loss/retry qualification defeats the candidate liveness claim.
counterevidence: Node.ReadIndex explicitly permits request loss without notice and requires retries with fresh contexts. Queue advancement can release earlier pending requests when a later request obtains a quorum.
limitations: No unconditional bounded completion requirement has been established. No state-machine read or stale value is claimed.

scope.description: Synchronous three-instance Raft test-network read-context probe with no dropped messages and no crashes.
assumptions: Initial voter membership is supplied by the existing newNetwork(nil,nil,nil) test constructor.
The existing test transport simulates completion of append dependencies without persisting durable bytes; the probe makes no crash-recovery claim.
Single-threaded ownership provides coherent observations of internal readStates, term, commit and pending queue.

experiment.prefix: Create three new Raft instances with the existing test constructor and empty logs; deliver a local campaign and all resulting actual election/append messages. Require leader state and a committed current-term entry before issuing the first read. Deliver all messages without filtering. Observe output in sequence independently of returned context. Send three local heartbeat triggers with full delivery, then a second unique nonempty read request. Repeat the same schedule in an independent network with a nonempty initial context.
